facts.text: Moose Jaw’s name may come from a 1857 survey calling the area Moose Jaw Bone Creek, or from a story of an Earl of Dunmore fixing cart with moose jawbone.
Moose Jaw’s Tunnels of Moose Jaw Tours let visitors explore historic tunnels that once housed Chinese workers and now host ghost stories and true crime tales.
The Moose Jaw WDM museum showcases transportation history and a Snowbirds gallery honoring the Royal Canadian Air Force’s wartime training base.
Lorne Calvert Campground, founded in 1927, remains North America’s longest‑running campground, offering a slice of early 20th‑century travel culture.
Moose Jaw’s vintage trolley tour spins through colorful history, weaving legends, ghost tales, and unexpected true crime into a single ride.
In 1881, the Canadian Pacific Railway chose Moose Jaw’s confluence of the Moose Jaw River and Thunder Creek as a division point, sparking the city’s growth.
